Definition: a sign of the object of a verb
BiblicalUsage: Yath is the Aramaic sign of the object, the small word that marks what a verb is done to. It stands once, in the accusation against Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego, where the Chaldeans say the king set these men over the affairs of Babylon.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe even the smallest words of Scripture are placed with care, and the object of the verb matters to God.
